title: Update quickstarts templates with first production launch steps + observability hooks
creator: Dylan Brooks
content:
## Context
We’re adding an in-Console guided onboarding checklist for Hosted API (Phase 1). Each checklist step must have a canonical docs link and a working quickstart path (Python/TypeScript/Go) that demonstrates the same best-practice patterns.

This ticket updates the **redwood-quickstarts** templates so that “first production launch” readiness items are not just described in docs, but are present in the default scaffolding. Goal: reduce support load (401/429/timeouts/stream disconnects), increase conversion to production keys, and make the path to production repeatable.

## Problem
Current quickstarts get users to a first successful response, but they do not consistently:
- Set explicit timeouts / retries with backoff and jitter
- Provide strong error guidance for common onboarding failures (401 wrong key env, 429 quotas, transient 5xx)
- Emit correlation IDs / request IDs and show how to use them in support tickets
- Offer minimal observability hooks (structured logs + optional OpenTelemetry)
- Distinguish dev/test vs prod keys and recommended env var conventions

These gaps show up in Support escalations and slow down “first production launch”.

## Goals / Non-goals
### Goals
- Update quickstart templates so that new projects start with production-sane defaults and instrumentation.
- Keep code patterns consistent across SDKs (auth, retries, streaming) per ENG-23121.
- Align copy and terminology with checklist step names (Console + docs).

### Non-goals
- Full Dedicated/Private deployment templates.
- Building a full monitoring stack; we only add lightweight hooks and documented integration points.

## Scope
Applies to: Hosted API quickstarts in **Python**, **TypeScript**, **Go** templates.

### 1) Production-readiness baseline (required)
Add (or ensure) the following in each template:
- **Timeouts**: explicit request timeout defaults (connect + overall) and guidance to tune.
- **Retries**: safe retry policy for transient errors:
  - Retry on: 408/409/425/429/5xx, network timeouts, stream reconnectable errors
  - Do not retry on: 401/403 (auth), 400 (validation) unless explicitly handled
  - Exponential backoff + jitter
  - Max retry count and max elapsed time
- **Error taxonomy & messaging**:
  - Print short actionable messages for 401 (wrong key or wrong env), 429 (quota/rate limit), timeouts, stream disconnect.
  - Include link placeholders to canonical troubleshooting docs (final URLs owned by Docs).
- **Key hygiene**:
  - Env var name conventions: REDWOOD_API_KEY (required), REDWOOD_ENV=(test|prod) optional.
  - Add README guidance: use a prod key for production; do not ship test keys.

### 2) Observability hooks (required)
- **Correlation ID logging**:
  - Log the request ID / trace ID returned by the API (or generated client-side if unavailable).
  - Include it in error logs and in the sample “contact support” block.
- **Structured logging**:
  - Log JSON with fields: timestamp, level, event, model, latency_ms, status, request_id.
  - Ensure we do not log customer prompt content by default.

### 3) Observability hooks (optional but included)
- **OpenTelemetry stub**:
  - Add a minimal optional integration section that shows how to create a span around an inference call.
  - Mark as optional with a clear “skip if you don’t use OTel”.

### 4) Checklist-aligned README updates
Update template README(s) to include a new section:
- “First production launch checklist (minimal)” (mirrors Confluence checklist definition)
- Link to the full docs page (“First production launch”) + troubleshooting

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Python/TS/Go templates all include explicit timeout + retry behavior and consistent copy.
- [x] Streaming example includes reconnect/disconnect guidance (at least: how to handle aborted streams and where to look for request_id).
- [x] Templates emit structured logs and correlation IDs without logging prompt content.
- [x] README includes a minimal production checklist section and links to canonical docs URLs.
- [x] Templates pass CI / compile checks in the quickstarts repo.

## Implementation plan
1) Audit current templates and identify drift vs doc snippets (coordinate with ENG-23121 owner).
2) Add shared guidance blocks to READMEs:
   - Retry policy, timeout tuning, key handling, and “do not log prompts”.
3) Update code samples:
   - Wrap API calls with retry helper
   - Capture response headers / metadata for request_id
   - Structured logger helper
4) Add optional OTel snippet:
   - Keep dependency optional; show pseudo-code if we can’t add deps without bloat.
5) Validate:
   - Run template smoke tests locally + CI.
   - Confirm copy matches checklist step titles from PRD/UX spec.

## Testing
- Template build/run smoke tests for each language.
- Manual checklist walkthrough:
  - Set invalid key => see 401 guidance
  - Force 429 scenario (low quota org) => see 429 guidance
  - Force timeout (low timeout) => confirm retry/backoff and request_id logged
  - Streaming disconnect simulation (close connection) => guidance appears

## Rollout / Comms
- Land as a quickstarts repo PR; no feature flag.
- Notify Docs/DevEx in #devex + link PR for copy alignment.
- Ensure Console checklist deep links point to updated template README anchors where applicable.

## Links
- Initiative: PM-482 Guided onboarding initiative
- Definition: PM-483 Define first production launch
- SDK parity: ENG-23121 SDK snippet parity python/ts/go
- Quickstarts PRs:
  - https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/604 (prod-readiness section + monitoring pointers)
  - https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/611 (first request + streaming guided steps, copy alignment)

## Open questions
- Final canonical docs URLs (Docs owns redirects/versioning). Track in ENG-23123 for deep-link versioning.
- Confirm source of request_id header naming across gateway/runtime (if header differs by region, standardize or fall back to client-generated UUID).

2026-02-07 (Ibrahim Khan): Retry/backoff defaults look good. Please ensure TypeScript sample uses the same retry-on status codes as Python. Also: do not retry on 400/401/403.
2026-02-10 (Dev Patel): +1 on making request_id obvious. In Support we keep asking for it; put it in the error output and in the ‘contact support’ snippet.
2026-02-14 (Nadia Rahman): Observability hook is fine, but please avoid logging prompts by default. If you need an example, use a placeholder prompt string and mention redaction explicitly.
2026-02-18 (Wei Chen): Implemented structured JSON logging helper (no prompt content). Added request_id extraction (fallback to UUID). Added optional OTel section as copy-only to avoid hard deps.
2026-03-06 (Dylan Brooks): Marking Done. Changes landed via quickstarts PRs #604 + #611. Follow-up tracked in ENG-23123 to lock docs deep links + redirects.
